==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:scheren|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|sheren}}, {{m|enm|scheren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċieran||to shear; to shave}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skeran}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skeraną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-|t=to cut}}.

Cognate with {{cog|fy|skarre}}, {{cog|nds,nl,de|scheren}}, {{cog|da|skære}}, {{cog|nb|skjære}}, {{cog|nn|skjera}}, {{cog|sv|skära}}, {{cog|fo,is|skera}}, (borrowed from Germanic) {{cog|fi|keritä|id=shear}}; and {{qualifier|from Indo-European}} with {{cog|bsh|ċarë́-|t=to chop}}, {{cog|grc|κείρω||to cut off}}, {{cog|la|caro||flesh}}, {{cog|sq|shqerr||to tear, cut}}, {{m|sq|harr||to cut, to mow}}, {{cog|lt|skìrti||separate}}, {{cog|cy|ysgar||separate}}. See also {{l|en|sharp}}.

===Verb===
{{en-verb|+|+|+,shore|shorn,~ed}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|transitive}} To [[remove]] the [[fleece#Noun|fleece]] from (a [[sheep]], [[llama]], etc.) by [[clip#Verb|clipping]].
#: {{syn|en|fleece#Verb}}
#: {{hyper|en|cut off#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|'''shear''' the llamas}}
# To [[cut]] the [[hair]] of (a person).
#: {{cot|en|shave#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|'''shear''' the afro off someone's head}}
# To [[cut]], originally with a sword or other bladed weapon, now usually with [[shears]], or as if using shears.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Sonnets|sonnet=68|passage=the golden tresses {{...}} were '''shorn''' away}}
# {{lb|en|physics}} To [[deform]] because of [[force]]s pushing in [[opposite]] [[direction]]s.
# {{lb|en|aviation|meteorology|intransitive|of [[wind]]}} To change in [[direction]] or [[speed]].
#* {{quote-book|en|date=21 March 1985|author=w:National Transportation Safety Board|title=Aircraft Accident Report: United Airlines Flight 663, Boeing 727-222, N7647U, Denver, Colorado, May 31, 1984|chapter=2.3 Airplane Takeoff Performance|url=https://libraryonline.erau.edu/online-full-text/ntsb/aircraft-accident-reports/AAR85-05.pdf|page=41|text=The total along-the-runway wind component '''sheared''' from an 8-knot headwind to about a 56-knot tailwind over a 44-second period.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260128094552/https://libraryonline.erau.edu/online-full-text/ntsb/aircraft-accident-reports/AAR85-05.pdf|archivedate=28 January 2026}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} To [[transform]] by [[displace|displacing]] every point in a [[direction]] [[parallel]] to some given [[line]] by a [[distance]] [[proportional]] to the point’s distance from the line.
# {{lb|en|mining|intransitive}} To make a [[vertical]] cut in [[coal]].
# {{lb|en|engineering}} (also 'shear off') To break or suddenly [[separate]] because of excessive [[force]], eg. a bolt.
# {{lb|en|Scotland}} To [[reap]], as grain.
# {{lb|en|figurative}} To [[deprive]] of [[property]]; to [[fleece]].

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# A cutting tool similar to [[scissors]], but often larger.
#: {{synonyms|en|shears}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Georgics|3|passage=short of their wool, and naked from the '''shear'''}}
# {{lb|en|metalworking}} A large machine use for cutting [[sheet metal]].
# The act of shearing, or something removed by shearing.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1837|author=w:William Youatt|title=Sheep: Their Breeds, Management, and Diseases
|passage=After the second shearing, he is a two-'''shear''' ram; {{...}} at the expiration of another year, he is a three-'''shear''' ram; the name always taking its date from the time of shearing.}}
# {{lb|en|physics}} [[force|Forces]] that push in opposite directions.
# {{lb|en|aviation|meteorology|uncountable}} The [[phenomenon]] of [[wind shear]].
#* {{quote-book|en|date=21 March 1985|author=w:National Transportation Safety Board|title=Aircraft Accident Report: United Airlines Flight 663, Boeing 727-222, N7647U, Denver, Colorado, May 31, 1984|chapter=2.3 Airplane Takeoff Performance|url=https://libraryonline.erau.edu/online-full-text/ntsb/aircraft-accident-reports/AAR85-05.pdf|page=41|text=The first effect of a wind shear was detected at 34 to 42 seconds into the takeoff, at a speed of about 115 KIAS with the airplane about 3,800 feet down the runway. An average '''shear''' rate of about 2.5 knots per second resulted in an interruption in acceleration at this point with the airspeed remaining at 115 to 120 KIAS for 7 to 10 seconds.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260128094552/https://libraryonline.erau.edu/online-full-text/ntsb/aircraft-accident-reports/AAR85-05.pdf|archivedate=28 January 2026}}
# {{lb|en|aviation|meteorology|countable}} A specific [[instance]] of [[wind shear]].
#: {{ux|en|We hit a nasty '''shear''' on approach and had to go around.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} A [[transformation]] that [[displace]]s every point in a [[direction]] [[parallel]] to some given [[line]] by a [[distance]] [[proportional]] to the point's distance from the line.
# {{lb|en|geology}} The response of a [[rock]] to [[deformation]] usually by [[compressive]] [[stress]], resulting in particular [[texture]]s.
